articles.title: Burnham's Breakneck First Week: A Northern Office, Tax Cuts, and a Message to the World
articles.summary: New UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham capped a whirlwind first week by opening a part-time office in Manchester, signaling his commitment to decentralizing power. He also announced tax cuts and faced foreign policy tests from Ukraine to Iran.

articles.title: Trump Returns to Correspondents' Dinner with Rambling Speech, Jabs, and a 'Trump 2028' Hat
articles.summary: At a rescheduled White House Correspondents' Dinner, President Trump delivered an hour-long mix of humor and insults, targeting journalists and political foes. He joked about a third term and donned a 'Trump 2028' cap, while security was tightened after April's shooting scare.

articles.title: Fact-Check: Can Foreign Adversaries Really Hack US Voting Machines?
articles.summary: Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin claimed foreign adversaries can access voting machines and flip votes. Experts acknowledge vulnerabilities but stress there's no evidence of such attacks in real elections, thanks to physical safeguards and paper ballots.
